title: Evaluating Bias in LLMs for Job-Resume Matching: Gender, Race, and Education

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual name substitution in candidate resumes using specific male and female names, followed by linear regression analysis with L1 regularization to measure the impact on LLM job-resume matching scores.

Counterfactual name substitution in candidate resumes using names statistically associated with different racial groups (White, Black or African American, Asian, Hispanic or Latino), and evaluating the effect on matching scores.

Substituting the names of educational institutions in candidate resumes across four distinct categories (Ivy League, HBCUs, Women's Colleges, and lesser-known colleges) to assess the influence of institutional prestige and type on LLM hiring decisions.

Using candidate names representing diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds from 8 different global locales (e.g., Spanish, English, Zulu, Twi, Japanese, Chinese) to assess cross-cultural preferences in resume evaluation.
